sentences: Click here to return to FAST Tap here to return to FAST FAST KUALA LUMPUR: Three male students were arrested over the alleged murder of a female schoolmate at a secondary school in Johor, as Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim called for a swift probe on Sunday (Oct 4).
Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim offered his condolences to the family of Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, who was found dead at a secondary school in Yong Peng, Johor.
The 16-year-old victim was among her school’s top students, a classmate who declined to be named told NST.
Earlier this month, a 15-year-old boy who stabbed and killed his schoolmate at a secondary school in Malaysia's Selangor state last October was ruled to be of unsound mind and acquitted of murder .
Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, 16, died after being found unconscious and covered in blood in a school hall in Yong Peng on Saturday, Bernama reported.
One of the three suspects, who are all 16, was brought to the Magistrate's Court in Johor on Sunday morning, where a six-day remand order was granted until Oct 9.
Police arrested the three suspects just hours after the victim's body was found, reported The Star.
The boy had no previous criminal record, according to Johor police chief Ab Rahaman Arsad.
The case is being investigated for murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
Faeza described her niece as a hardworking, quiet and kind student who consistently excelled academically.
"We can still picture her face and never imagined we would lose her," the classmate told NST.

Travelling overseas I need help overseas Visiting Singapore Careers Newsroom About MFA eRegister trip (opens in new tab) Home About MFA Key issues Pedra Branca Pedra Branca Comprehensive overview of the Pedra Branca territorial dispute between Singapore and Malaysia.
Beginnings of the dispute In 1979, Malaysia published a map [JPEG, 156 KB] ↗ (opens in new tab) which claimed the island as hers.
In response, Singapore lodged a formal protest with Malaysia in early 1980, to assert that Pedra Branca belonged to Singapore.
Malaysia accepted this proposal in 1994.
The ICJ was requested to determine whether sovereignty over (a) Pedra Branca; (b) Middle Rocks; and (c) South Ledge belonged to Malaysia or Singapore.

Written and oral proceedings In accordance with the terms of the Special Agreement, the ICJ scheduled [PDF, 332 KB] ↗ (opens in new tab) three rounds of written pleadings, which were to be exchanged simultaneously.
Both Singapore and Malaysia made oral arguments before the ICJ from 6-23 November 2007.
Furthermore, in 1953, Johor stated in official correspondence [JPEG, 71 KB] ↗ (opens in new tab) with Singapore that it did not claim ownership over the island.
Malaysia also published a series of official maps [JPEG, 574 KB] ↗ (opens in new tab) from 1962 to 1975 depicting Pedra Branca as belonging to Singapore.

In the case of Pedra Branca, the ICJ held that while the Sultanate of Johor had original title to Pedra Branca, sovereignty over the island had passed to Singapore by 1980 (when the dispute crystallised).

This was demonstrated by the concrete acts of sovereignty conducted over the island by Singapore and its predecessors, taken together with the failure of Malaysia and its predecessors to respond to these acts.
Post-judgment After the ICJ’s Judgment was released, both Singapore and Malaysia agreed to abide by the ICJ’s ruling.

A ‘Malaysia-Singapore Joint Technical Committee on the Implementation of the ICJ Judgment on Pedra Branca, Middle Rocks and South Ledge’ (MSJTC) was formed by both countries to implement the ICJ’s Judgment.
On 2 February 2017, Malaysia filed an application for revision of the ICJ’s 2008 Judgment.
Singapore filed its Written Observations on the admissibility of Malaysia’s revision application with the ICJ on 24 May 2017.

Malaysia subsequently filed its Additional Written Observations on 11 December 2017, following which Singapore filed its Written Comments on Malaysia's Additional Written Observations on 12 February 2018.
On 30 June 2017, Malaysia filed a request for interpretation of the ICJ’s 2008 Judgment.
Malaysia’s request for interpretation was additional to, and separate from, its revision application.
Singapore filed its Written Observations on Malaysia's request for interpretation of the ICJ's 2008 Judgement with the ICJ on 30 October 2017.
Malaysia subsequently filed its Written Comments on Singapore's Written Observations on 15 February 2018.
Thereafter, Singapore filed its Written Response to Malaysia's Written Comments on 23 April 2018.
On 28 May 2018, Malaysia informed the ICJ that it would discontinue the proceedings for both the revision and interpretation cases that it had initiated earlier.
On 29 May 2018, Singapore informed the ICJ that it agreed with Malaysia's request for discontinuance.

On the same day, the ICJ informed Malaysia and Singapore that the Court had placed on record the discontinuance, by agreement of the Parties, of both sets of proceedings instituted by Malaysia against Singapore, and directed that the cases be removed from the Court's list.
